analysis.title: Wall Street's Midterm Cheat Sheet: The Likeliest Outcome Is The Worst For Stocks
key_insights: Prediction markets have Democrats at a 66% chance of taking both the House and Senate (JPM Market Intelligence, Bloomberg prediction market data as of Nov 1). A Democratic sweep is the only scenario in which JPM's S&P 500 range includes a decline (-0.25% to +0.50%).
JPM's S&P 500 reaction ranges by outcome: Dem House with GOP Senate (26% odds) +0.50% to +1.00%, GOP sweep (7%) +1.00% to +1.25%, GOP House with Dem Senate (1%) +0.25% to +0.75%.
Democratic sweep odds rose from 62% in early October to 66%. The Dem House with GOP Senate split fell from 29% to 26%.

On AI regulation, JPM thinks a Democratic sweep would struggle to pass limits because Trump has said he will not sign bills limiting AI and Democrats cannot reach a veto-proof majority. JPM calls a post-election dip a buying opportunity for AI bulls, with the risk that the market de-grosses within the AI theme.

Goldman (Phillips and Duggirala) also expects a modest burden on AI companies, centered on self-directed testing and self-regulation, and sees a nationwide data center moratorium as unlikely in any outcome. It expects a Democratic chamber to open investigations into large tech companies and to push to exclude data centers from bonus depreciation and R&D credits. Democrats could float a federal gross receipts tax or an excise tax on data center electricity use.
JPM flags 'investigation risk' for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including megacap tech, citing the WSJ.

The banks differ on the deficit. JPM expects lower deficit spending under a Blue Wave or split Congress, which could pull long-end yields slightly lower, and higher long-end yields under a Red Wave. Goldman expects spending to rise slightly under Democrats.

Goldman cites Democratic proposals to reverse last year's spending cuts (about $85 billion in 2027, or 0.25% of GDP, mostly Medicaid at $55 billion and nutrition programs at $18 billion) and to reinstate expanded ACA subsidies (about $50 billion a year).
Government funding expires Dec. 11, and Goldman expects Congress to push it to February or March. The debt limit is likely to bind by October 2027 at the latest.

Goldman expects Trump to release Section 301 overcapacity findings after the election. Combined with the existing 10-12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariff, this would restore partner tariff rates to roughly their level before the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs, raising the US effective tariff rate by a little under 2 percentage points.

JPM says a Red Wave may embolden Trump to continue in Iran until a US-friendly deal or Iranian capitulation. A Democratic Congress could cut funding or force troop removal after 90 days without approval, but not before January.

JPM argues crude has already priced a resumption of hostilities. The 2027 WTI fair-value swap trades around $88 against normal prices of $65-70 (Henrici), and Brent is about $20 a barrel above fundamentals (Kaneva). JPM says adding some downside protection 'may be prudent'. Goldman just raised its Brent forecasts on supply disruption risk.

JPM cites AP and WSJ reports verified by satellite imagery that Iran damaged 119 buildings across 13 US installations in the first two weeks of the war. With depleted munitions, JPM thinks another wave of US strikes would be limited in scope and duration.

More than 43 million Americans had voted early as of last Wednesday, nearly 10 million more than 2022. About 6.8 million Democrats and 5.2 million Republicans have voted in states reporting party, but early voting skews Democratic.

Goldman reads prediction markets as giving Democrats better than 90% odds in the House and better than 65% in the Senate, with markets implying about 236 Democratic House seats. National sentiment has moved 10-11 points toward Democrats since 2024.

Senate polling risk: since 2002, GOP Senate candidates in Republican-leaning states have beaten final polling margins by an average of 3 points, and candidates leading by 2.5 points or less in competitive races won only 60% of the time. Democrats lead by more than 3 points in a Republican-held seat only in North Carolina.

The banks read voter priorities differently. JPM cites CNBC and Fox News polls showing corruption has overtaken affordability as the top issue. Goldman's Harris Poll data has cost of living far ahead, corruption a distant second and AI the top issue for 2% of voters.

The S&P 500 has been higher one year after every midterm since 1950, averaging about 15%. The worst case, after 1986, reflected the 1987 crash. JPM's averages after a midterm are +5.4% at 3 months, +11.4% at 6 months, +12.5% at 9 months and +14.7% at 12 months, with 6, 9 and 12-month returns positive every time since 1990.
JPM's Delta One team says its Split Congress pair has rallied to two-year highs.

Goldman expects a Democratic Senate win to push Trump to make personnel changes quickly so a Republican majority can confirm them before year-end. Trump can name acting officials at cabinet agencies but not at independent agencies such as the Federal Reserve or the courts.

sector_views.rationale: JPM calls a post-election AI dip a buying opportunity, with risk of de-grossing within the AI theme. Goldman expects only a modest regulatory burden but a possible loss of data center tax breaks.
JPM says crude already prices a resumption of hostilities, with WTI 2027 swaps near $88 and Brent about $20 above fundamentals. Goldman raised its Brent forecasts on supply disruption risk.

De-grossing within the AI theme after the election.
Democratic investigations into large technology companies and loss of data center tax breaks.
Investigation risk for Trump-linked donors, including megacap tech, and for Elon Musk.
Post-midterm escalation in Iran and the Gulf.
Tariff increases from Section 301 actions after the election.
Government funding deadline on Dec. 11 and the debt limit binding by October 2027.
Senate polling misses: GOP candidates have beaten final polling margins by an average of 3 points since 2002.
vol_and_positioning: JPM says equity investors have fewer oil hedges to offset losses because crude already prices escalation, and that adding some downside protection 'may be prudent'.
JPM's Delta One team says its Split Congress pair has rallied to two-year highs.
JPM flags the risk that the market de-grosses within the AI theme after the election.
A related headline cited in the piece says UBS warns of a year-end squeeze with near-record shorts.
geopolitical: US-Iran war running past 90 days without congressional approval. A Democratic Congress could cut funding or force troop removal, but not until January.
Iran damaged 119 buildings across 13 US installations in the first two weeks of the war (AP and WSJ, verified with satellite imagery).
JPM thinks another wave of US strikes would be limited in scope and duration given depleted munitions, which may point to heightened diplomatic efforts.
Oil market bracing for post-midterm escalation in the Gulf.
Section 301 overcapacity investigation findings expected after the election, with possible Democratic efforts to unwind tariffs on Canadian imports.
cross_bank_references: JPM and Goldman land in the same place on AI regulation.
The two banks part ways on what a Democratic Congress means for the deficit: JPM expects lower deficit spending, Goldman expects slightly higher spending.
The banks read voters differently: JPM points to corruption overtaking affordability, Goldman's Harris Poll data has cost of living far ahead.
